title: Arctic Question 1
scenario: The Arctic is one of Earth's polar regions.
question: Where is the Arctic?

options.text: At the south of the planet
options.explanation: The south polar region is called the Antarctic, not the Arctic.

options.text: At the north of the planet
options.explanation: The Arctic is Earth's northern polar region, around the North Pole.
The Equator is the warm middle line around Earth, far from the polar Arctic region.

title: Arctic Question 2
scenario: The Arctic and Antarctic are both cold polar regions, but they are not the same kind of place.
question: The Arctic is:

options.explanation: Antarctica is a continent. The Arctic is mainly ocean covered by sea ice.
This describes a land-centred region, but the Arctic is centred on an ocean.

options.text: A cold ocean surrounded by land
options.explanation: The Arctic is the Arctic Ocean, covered by sea ice and surrounded by northern land areas.

title: Arctic Question 3
scenario: Scientists can study Arctic sea ice over many years by observing it from above.
question: How was the sea-ice age data collected?

options.text: From satellites looking at the ocean
options.explanation: Satellites observe sea ice from space, helping scientists map and track changes across the Arctic Ocean.
A measuring stick or tape cannot measure sea-ice age across the whole Arctic Ocean.
Laboratory work can help study samples, but this type of large-scale sea-ice age data comes from satellite observations.

title: Arctic Question 4
scenario: Arctic sea ice grows during the cold dark winter and melts during the warmer summer.
question: Which month has the most sea ice?

options.explanation: Arctic sea ice usually reaches its yearly maximum around March, after the winter freezing season.
By June, the Arctic has entered the melt season, so sea ice is usually decreasing.
October is after the summer minimum, when sea ice starts growing again, but it is not usually the maximum month.

title: Arctic Question 5
scenario: Some years have much less Arctic sea ice than others, especially in more recent decades.
question: Which years have the least sea ice?

options.explanation: This group includes years that are not the lowest sea-ice years in the dataset.
These are the years identified in the activity as having the least sea ice.
This group does not match the least sea-ice years identified in the activity.
